title: Delta Air Lines says system issue that delayed flights nationwide has been resolved | CNN
text:
Source: CNN

Delta Air Lines has resolved an issue with its weight and balance system that caused nationwide delays leading into a busy Thanksgiving travel week, the airline said.

Calculating weight and balance on an aircraft is a critical part of the pre-departure preparations. Delta was forced to use “manual workarounds” on Sunday morning “to safely get flights departed,” the airlinetold CNN affiliate WSB-TV, as delays rippled across its network.

The system’s automation for departing flight weight and balance calculations is now working, Delta said. But passengers could still experience lingering effects from the holdup.

Over half of Delta’s total flights were delayed and 6% were canceled as of 9:30 p.m. ET on Sunday, according to flight tracking websiteFlightAware.Delta has said about 70% of Sunday’s schedule changes were due to the automation issue, which caused an hourslong ground delay at Hartsfield-Jackson Atlanta International Airport – Delta’s biggest travel hub and thebusiest airport in the world.

The ground delay was canceled around 11:30 a.m. ET, according to anFAA advisory.

“Delta teams are focused on completing the remainder of today’s schedule. Cancellations, as always, are a last resort when all other options have been exhausted,” Delta told CNN, apologizing to customers for the delay in their travels.

Calculating weight and balance on an aircraft ensures the fully loaded aircraft is not too heavy to fly, is loaded properly and the pilots have the right settings for a safe takeoff.

Major airlines use sophisticated computer programs at their headquarters to calculate these numbers.

“Compliance with the weight and balance limits of any aircraft is critical to flight safety,” according to theFAA’s Pilot’s Handbook of Aeronautical Knowledge.

For Delta, the weight and balance instructions for baggage crews are planned at the Operations and Customer Center in the Atlanta headquarters using a system called ALIS, or Automated Load Instruction System.

“Right now, it’s a system-wide outage for Delta Air Lines,” an employee explained to a pilot in Boston on Sunday morning in a radio call captured byATC.com. “The ramp isn’t really able to load because there is no ramp worksheet in there, so that’s what we’re doing, we’re manually counting bags and doing a report for you guys.”

“Oh, geez,” the pilot responded.

“Kinda like the good old days across here,” the ramp worker noted sarcastically.

The Delta slowdowns come at the outset of what is projected to be a busy holiday travel period.Over four million travelersare expected at Delta’s Atlanta hub between November 19 and December 1, according to a news release from the airport.

Many travelers have already experienced long lines and frustrating disruptions in recent weeks afterall flights nationwide were groundedjust over a week ago, sparking flight delays and cancellations for several days.

The FAA has said the outages that triggered the nationwide ground stop likely stemmed from an outdated copper wire at a remote location.

Sunday’s Delta delays are not related to any FAA air traffic systems, the FAA confirmed in asocial media post.

The ground delay affected Delta flights and was not airport-wide, a spokesperson for Hartsfield-Jackson told CNN in a statement.

More than 60% of flights out of Hartsfield-Jackson were delayed Sunday evening, according toFlightAware,while around half of inbound flights to the airport were also delayed. The data does not specify how many of these delays were Delta flights.

Atlanta resident Shane Rocha and her family were traveling through Hartsfield-Jackson on Sunday morning to visit family, Rocha told CNN affiliate WANF. Rocha said she had flown earlier in the week without any issues and was hoping that today’s travel would be equally smooth.

“Luckily we’re only 19 minutes delayed, knock on wood,” she said. “Hopefully it stays that low.”

Although the specifics surrounding the Delta issue remain unclear,United Airlines experienced an issuewith its weight and balance computer system in 2025 that triggered more than 1,000 delays and dozens of cancellations, the airline said at the time.

United also experienced abrief system outageon November 16 that affected fewer than 150 flights across the US, the airline told CNN. This outage appears unrelated to Sunday’s Delta automation issue and the previous nationwide FAA ground stop.

At the time of United’s outage, the FAA said the incident was not an agency equipment issue and the airline said there is no indication it was cybersecurity-related.

Beyond system disruptions,severe weatherin the Northeastern United States has caused headaches as many people travel for the upcoming Thanksgiving holiday.

Passengers flying to New York’s LaGuardia Airport and New Jersey’s Newark Liberty International Airport can expect around two hours of weather-related ground delays on average,according to FAA updates.

Weather has also sparked delays for flights to San Francisco, while San Diego and several Florida airports are experiencing departure hold-ups due to a high volume of flights.

This story has been updated with additional information.
